thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: autoscaler.high_queue_backlog for service=inference-autoscaler · urgency=high · PD: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD-12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident PD-12345 triggered (ack required) · Alerts: queue_length > 5000 for 5m, pending_requests rising · runbook: /runbooks/autoscaler-backlog

maya (oncall): acked in PD · I'm on it, pulling dashboards now. seeing queue spike across us-east-1 compute-cell-3 :eyes:

maya (oncall): graphs: request queue went from 200 -> 6200 in ~2m. worker provision lag ~30s, pod creation pending due to quota errors on nodepool-autoscale.

carl: @maya can you paste the HPA/scale target? could be minReplica cap hit or node quota.

maya (oncall): HPA: inference-autoscaler-hpa target=500 rps, currentReplicas=4, max=10. Cluster nodepool quotas at 12 nodes, currently 12 used. kubectl describe shows Pending scheduling due to insufficient cpu.

ashley: copy — looks like nodepool quota exhausted. we hit provider limit, autoscaler can't add nodes. opening provider quota request will be slow (>10m). Need short-term mitigation.

ops-lead: mitigation options: 1) manual routing to fall back model-variant smaller (cpu) 2) throttle burst traffic upstream (gateway) 3) temporarily increase per-pod concurrency to reduce pod count 4) manual scale of replica CPU-limited pods if scheduling allows to burst on already provisioned nodes.

maya (oncall): trying option 3 first — bump concurrency via configmap for async-worker: set MAX_CONCURRENCY=48 -> rolling restart. applying now:

maya (oncall): ```kubectl set env deployment/inference-worker MAX_CONCURRENCY=48 -n infra-prod && kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker -n infra-prod```

infra-bot: rollout started: inference-worker (3/3 updated) · new pods scheduling on existing nodes.

maya (oncall): concurrency change applied. seeing backlog growth slow but still ~3k pending. some customers report 5-20s latency, <1% 504s. tagging customer-impact.

carl: we should also open manual burst capacity via reserved spot: can we spin up a temporary small nodepool (cpu-only) to relieve scheduling? aws-bastion team can approve quick.

ashley: i'll request quick-provision nodepool-small-ephemeral with 6 nodes; ETA 4-6m. Meanwhile enable fallback routing for less critical tenants.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step: If node quota prevents autoscale, trigger manual nodepool creation: /infra/create-ephemeral-nodepool --name nodepool-ephemeral --count 6 --type c5.large · Confirmed by infra policy: expedited.

ops-lead: @carl @maya coordinate customer comms. _Which customers impacted?_ maya: dashboards show high QPS from account: acme-corp and beta-voice-app. reach out to SE for status page note.

maya (oncall): posting short status: "We are experiencing degraded inference throughput in us-east-1 due to capacity exhaustion. Automated autoscaler is unable to provision nodes because of nodepool quota. Mitigations in progress: increased per-pod concurrency and provisioning ephemeral nodes. Expected recovery ~10-15m." linking status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INF-2026-03

pagerduty: PD escalation: second oncall required · escalation to carl (SRE-II) performed.

carl: nodepool-ephemeral creation approved by infra, provisioning started. checking scheduler events: pods starting to bind as nodes come up.

infra-bot: nodepool-ephemeral ready: 6 nodes registered. kube-scheduler reports backlog draining.

maya (oncall): backlog falling: pending_requests -> 400 -> 120 over 3m. latency trending back to baseline. continuing to monitor.

ops-lead: great. next: follow-up actions: 1) file provider quota increase 2) add alert for nodepool-utilization to catch quota saturation earlier 3) evaluate autoscaler target/limits and burst policy 4) postmortem.

ashley: opened ticket INF-464 (quota request) and PM linked.

maya (oncall): handing off to @emma (next-oncall) for monitoring during the cool-down window. leaving notes: increased concurrency, ephemeral nodepool created/removed? we'll deprovision once backlog < 50 for 10m.

emma (next-oncall): acked — taking watch. will follow cleanup steps and update postmortem with timeline and customer impact numbers.

carl: one quick note — need a follow-up to tune HPA max/min and consider burst nodepool autoscaler policy so autoscaler can create ephemeral spot pools automatically.

incident-bot: PD-12345 resolved by maya (ack) & carl (escalation) · incident status: mitigated -> monitoring · duration: ~18m.

maya (oncall): closing thread in ~10m if stable. will file the postmortem draft with metrics and runbook gaps. :memo:
